continuities.name: Naruto anime (TV series and canon films)
continuities.description: The Pierrot TV anime (Naruto, Naruto: Shippuden, Boruto: Naruto Next Generations) plus the two films Wikipedia calls part of the canonical storyline (The Last, Boruto: Naruto the Movie). Kept apart from the manga because the anime adds original (filler) storylines. No calendar years exist; order is story order, with filler placed where it airs.
continuities.quote: The episodes are based on the first twenty-seven volumes in Part I of the manga, while some episodes feature original, self-contained storylines. … [Boruto: Naruto the Movie] is the second film to be a part of the canonical Naruto storyline, being a sequel to the manga series.

continuities.name: Naruto manga
continuities.description: Masashi Kishimoto's Naruto manga and its sequel manga Boruto (Naruto Next Generations, Two Blue Vortex). Separate from the anime, which adds filler and (for Boruto) an original prequel opening.
continuities.quote: It is a spin-off and sequel to Kishimoto's manga series Naruto … Unlike the manga, which begins as a retelling of the Boruto film, the anime starts as a prequel set before Boruto and his friends become ninjas.

continuities.name: Naruto anime films (non-canon)
continuities.description: The nine original-story theatrical films (2004–2012). Each is set "after episode N" of the anime, but none is part of the canonical storyline, so they are ordered only among themselves by that stated placement.
continuities.quote: [Boruto: Naruto the Movie] is the second film to be a part of the canonical Naruto storyline … Naruto was adapted into 11 theatrical films. The first three films correspond to the first anime series, and the remaining eight correspond to the second.
continuities.note: Wikipedia never uses the word "non-canon" for these nine films; the status is inferred from the Boruto film being "the second film to be a part of the canonical Naruto storyline" (the first being The Last), which leaves the other nine outside it.

continuities.name: One Piece anime (TV series and Oda-era films)
continuities.description: Toei's 1999 TV anime, ordered by story/airing (seasons = Wikipedia story arcs, anime-original arcs where they air), plus the five films the brief treats as canon/semi-canon (Strong World, Z, Gold, Stampede, Red), each placed next to its TV tie-in arc. Wikipedia does NOT call these films canon (see film notes), so their placement is "disputed". No numbered years exist in the story.
continuities.quote: | auxA5 = TV Original … With the release of films ten, twelve, thirteen, and fourteen, tie-in story arcs of the TV series were aired concurrently.

continuities.name: One Piece manga
continuities.description: Eiichiro Oda's manga, the source text. Separate from the anime (which has anime-original arcs) and from the films (Oda "does not connect the films to his manga").
continuities.quote: He stated that he does not connect the films to his manga, as doing so would make outside material effectively obligatory

continuities.name: One Piece anime films (non-canon)
continuities.description: The ten earlier theatrical films (2000–2011) with original or retold stories. Wikipedia says the films cannot share one continuity, so they are ordered by release only.
continuities.quote: They feature self-contained, completely original plots, or alternate retellings of story arcs with animation of a higher quality than that of the regular anime series. … The films themselves offer contradictions in both chronology and design that make them incompatible with a single continuity.

continuities.name: One Piece (Netflix live-action)
continuities.description: Netflix's live-action adaptation; its own continuity, retelling the manga from East Blue.
continuities.quote: The series is a live-action adaptation of the 1997 Japanese manga series One Piece by Eiichiro Oda, who also serves as a creative consultant.

titles.title: One Piece Film: Strong World

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: Eventually, the film premiered on December 12, 2009. | released = {{Film date|2009|12|12}}

in_universe.label: between Thriller Bark and Sabaody (fan wiki)
in_universe.quote: This movie would be chronologically set after the Thriller Bark Arc and before the Sabaody Archipelago Arc, as Brook is part of the Straw Hats and the whole crew remains together.
in_universe.note: Fan-wiki placement (One Piece Wiki, secondary). Conflict: the TV prologue "A Gold Lion's Ambition" (eps 426–429, season 13) is "set outside the current continuity" (One Piece season 13, Wikipedia), and Oda says he "does not connect the films to his manga". Placed after season 10 (Thriller Bark).

titles.notes: Canon status per Wikipedia: not canon. "Oda addressed the canonicity of the film in 2024 … He stated that he does not connect the films to his manga". Oda was executive producer/story writer per the article. TV prologue: episodes 426–429.

titles.title: One Piece Film: Z

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: The 12th One Piece film was released on December 15, 2012. | released = {{Film date|2012|12|15}}

in_universe.label: end of season 15 (after Fish-Man Island)
in_universe.quote: The events of the film takes place near the end of the fifteenth season of the One Piece anime series during the "Z's Ambition" story arc, which serves as a prologue.
in_universe.note: Placement is stated by Wikipedia, but the film's canon status is not (and the One Piece article says the films are "incompatible with a single continuity"), so confidence is disputed.

titles.notes: Canon status: Wikipedia makes no canon claim; the One Piece article says the films "offer contradictions in both chronology and design that make them incompatible with a single continuity". TV prologue "Z's Ambition" = final four episodes of season 15.

titles.title: One Piece Film: Gold

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: The film was released in Japan on July 23, 2016, by its distributor Toei Company … | released = {{film date|2016|7|15|Emirates Palace|2016|7|23|Japan}}

in_universe.label: after Dressrosa, before Zou
in_universe.quote: It takes place after the Dressrosa Arc (Gild Tesoro stated that Luffy had beaten Donquixote Doflamingo and Sabo has the powers of the Mera Mera no Mi), and before the Zou Arc
in_universe.note: Fan-wiki placement (secondary), which also says "Like most other films, this movie cannot be properly set in any point of the canon story." Wikipedia (One Piece season 18): the "Silver Mine" arc that opens season 18 "serves as an introduction to the events of the film". Placed after season 17 (Dressrosa).

titles.notes: World premiere July 15, 2016 (Emirates Palace, Abu Dhabi); Japan July 23, 2016 used as release_date. Canon status: no canon claim in Wikipedia. TV prologue: "Silver Mine" arc (season 18).

titles.title: One Piece: Stampede

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: The 14th One Piece film was released on August 9, 2019. | released = {{Film date|2019|08|01|premiere|2019|08|09|Japan}}

in_universe.label: start of season 20 (before Wano proper)
in_universe.quote: Episodes 895 and 896 contain an original story arc, "Cidre Guild" which ties into the film One Piece: Stampede. … Other Supernovas make their way as, elsewhere, Buena Festa looks forward to a clash between Luffy and Douglas Bullet, leading to the events in One Piece: Stampede.
in_universe.note: Episodes 895–896 sit at the start of season 20 (episodes 892 onward), so the film is placed between seasons 19 and 20. Canon status not claimed by Wikipedia; disputed for the same reason as the other films.

titles.notes: Premiere August 1, 2019; Japan release August 9, 2019 used. Canon status: no canon claim in Wikipedia.

titles.title: One Piece Film: Red

units.label: Film
units.release_quote: The 15th One Piece film was released on August 6, 2022. | released = {{film date|2022|7|22|Tokyo premiere|2022|8|6|Japan}}

in_universe.label: after Wano (fan wiki)
in_universe.quote: The events of the film, while not canon, would likely take place after the Wano Country Arc, given that Jinbe is part of and sailing with the Straw Hat Pirates
in_universe.note: Fan-wiki placement (secondary; it calls the film "not canon"). Wikipedia only says tie-in episodes 1029–1030 ("Uta's Past", a flashback) aired after the film's release, mid-season 20. Placed after season 20 (Wano).

titles.notes: Tokyo premiere July 22, 2022; Japan release August 6, 2022 used. Canon status: Wikipedia makes no canon claim; the One Piece Wiki says "while not canon". Wikipedia (List of One Piece films) says the upcoming Film: God Valley "will be the first canon One Piece movie", implying Red is not.
